# Installer reference

**Step-by-step instructions for sandbox installs are in `BrightPAS-Installation-Guide-<version>.docx`** (shipped with every release, generated by `scripts/docs/install-guide.js`). It covers a single server (Windows Server + SQL Server 2022 + IIS + BrightPAS) tested from a Windows 11 workstation, written for junior IT staff. This page is the short technical reference.

## Menu (run `BrightPAS-Setup-<version>.exe` as administrator)
1. **Check this server** – read-only prerequisite checks with plain-English fixes.
2. **Install or upgrade BrightPAS** – 12 idempotent steps (below).
3. **Preview** – lists what install would do; changes nothing.
4. **Security, penetration and audit self-test** – read-only; HTML + text report in `C:\ProgramData\BrightPAS\Reports` (ADR 0007).
5. **Collect diagnostics** – one zip in `C:\ProgramData\BrightPAS\Support` (copy next to Setup.exe): Setup logs, reports, Hosting Bundle log, filtered Application/System event logs, IIS sites/app pool/bindings, certificates, folder ACLs, firewall, listening ports, SQL services, deployed `web.config`/`appsettings*.json`. Passwords masked. Offered automatically after any failed run.

## Install steps
Check server → install IIS (minimal features) → TLS 1.2/1.3 only → harden IIS → create database → schema scripts (core, identity, patients; audit ledger) → one-time first-admin code (shown once, never logged, 7 days) → .NET 10 Hosting Bundle (from `dotnet-hosting-10.*-win.exe` next to Setup) → application database login → deploy `BrightPAS-Web-<version>.zip` to `C:\Program Files\BrightPAS\Web` → IIS site/app pool, HTTPS only → health check.

**Single server** (SQL on `localhost`): the site connects as `IIS APPPOOL\BrightPAS` (Windows auth, db_datareader/db_datawriter) – no password exists. **Separate SQL server:** a generated `brightpas_app` SQL login, or `--app-windows-login DOMAIN\GMSA$` (ADR 0008).

## Logging
Every run writes `C:\ProgramData\BrightPAS\Logs\BrightPAS-<Install|Preview|Check|SecurityTest|Diagnostics>-<date>.log` (copy next to Setup.exe): header (OS, user, args, time zone), system probe, every step with timing, every SQL batch and PowerShell script/output, full exception details. Secrets are masked. `--verbose` shows the same detail on screen.

## Command line
```
Setup.exe check          [--sql-server NAME[:PORT]] [--drive C:\]
Setup.exe install        --sql-server NAME [--database BrightPAS] [--sql-user USER] [--trust-server-certificate]
                         [--skip-iis] [--skip-web] [--what-if] [--ignore-prerequisites] [--web-package PATH]
                         [--install-dir PATH] [--host-name NAME] [--https-port 443] [--certificate-thumbprint THUMB]
                         [--app-windows-login DOMAIN\ACCOUNT$] [--sms-provider Modica|GenericHttp|TestOutbox|Off]
                         [--email-provider Smtp|TestOutbox|Off]
Setup.exe security-test  [--url https://server/] [--sql-server NAME] [--database BrightPAS] [--no-rate-limit-tests]
Setup.exe diagnostics
Common: --verbose  --quiet
```
With `--quiet --sql-user`, the password comes from `BRIGHTPAS_SQL_PASSWORD` (never on the command line).
Exit codes: 0 OK · 1 warnings · 2 failed/not ready · 3 unexpected error.

## Messaging vendors (0.6.0)
Setup asks which SMS vendor and email sender the reminders module uses (Enter keeps the current choice; new installations default to **Modica** and **SMTP**). The choice is written to `appsettings.Production.json` (`Reminders:SmsProvider`, `Reminders:EmailProvider`) and applied to an existing `reminders.Settings` row. Vendor passwords are entered only in BrightPAS (SMS & email → Settings) and stored encrypted.
